description: Reality Check: Collaborative Research Contributes to Real-Life Policy Decisions is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Pacific Islands Climate Adaptation Science Center | Manager Climate Corps; County of Hawai'i Planning Department; University of Hawai'i at Hilo | Spatial Data Analysis and Visualization Labs. The research combined historic aerial photos, drone imagery, and topographic surveys to characterize coastal change around Hawai'i Island. The results are informing policy makers who are crafting a new setback policy for coastal development. Coverage: the United States (2019). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
